text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- India has eased travel restrictions on Pakistani nationals and offered other concessions in a goodwill gesture on the eve of next week's landmark talks between the two countries.
- At least 10 people were killed when a tremor measuring 4.5 on the Richter scale jolted the remote village of Salarzai in Bajaur Agency in North West Frontier Province of Pakistan.

- The Mohajir National Movement's nominee for the federal cabinet refused to take oath at the last minute after the ruling Pakistan Muslim League failed to announce his portfolio beforehand, a government source said.
- The government intends to hold local body elections after June, reliable sources said.
- Army took over security arrangements for the Organisation of Islamic Conference summit and troops have been deployed in the Islamabad for security.
- At least 16 Pakistanis on the fishing boat Al-Tabassum were arrested by Indian coast guards in the Arabian Sea.
- Tehmina Durrani, the controversial Pakistani author, will receive the prestigious Bellisario Award of Italy on Friday.

- Talks between senior Pakistani officials and the International Monertary Fund team to finalise modalities for release of another tranche of $130 million to Pakistan are progressing satisfactorily, sources said.
- The Privatisation Commission has proposed changes in incentives for transferring ownership of public sector units to employees.
- The High Commissioner of Kenya to Islamabad B.K. Kisilu has urged Pakistani businessmen to increase exports to Kenya which is still an untapped market.
- Federal Investment Bonds are fast losing ground as a fund raising instrument to Short Term Federal Bonds largely due to their lower yield on longer maturities.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The World Bank and other donor agencies will not disburse a $400 million loan to Pakistan if provincial assemblies do not enact ordinances on provincial irrigation and drainage authorities.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif will announce an economic package for relief of the common man after March 26.
THE NEWS
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the increase in the fiscal deficit has brought Pakistan to the brink of a financial emergency.

- At least 1,400 employees of state-run Pakistan International Airlines employed during the government of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto were sacked to curtail financial losses of the national flag carrier.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
